source: FinNLP 2025 @ EMNLP — Hadlock, Roberts, Lee (Tennessee Tech)
title: H304: LLM-Augmented PEAD — GPT-4o-mini Abstractive Summary + Sentence-BERT Embeddings
rationale: FinNLP 2025 (EMNLP) paper tests BART, FinBERT, and LLaMA 3.2-3B on 10-Q MD&A sections for PEAD signal. FinBERT achieves highest classification accuracy (57.6-58.3%); BART produces the best BHAR (3.29% 60-day in positive-earnings group). NOTE: the GPT-4o-mini + sentence-BERT design in this proposal is a design EXTENSION of the paper's direction (abstractive summarization → scoring), not a direct replication — the paper does not test GPT-4o-mini or SBERT. Our H163/H174 pipeline already uses FinBERT on 8-K filings. The extension hypothesis: if BART-style abstractive compression improves signal quality over raw 8-K text, then GPT-4o-mini (stronger abstraction) + sentence-BERT embeddings should do similarly or better, at lower inference cost. Two variants to test: (A) GPT-4o-mini abstractive summary → FinBERT score, (B) GPT-4o-mini abstractive summary → sentence-BERT cosine similarity. Gate: OOS win-rate > 81.8% (H174 baseline) OR mean return > 6.89%.

content.description: LLM-Augmented PEAD — GPT-4o-mini + sentence-BERT vs H174 FinBERT baseline
variants: A: GPT-4o-mini abstractive summary → FinBERT score on summary (not raw 8-K)
B: GPT-4o-mini abstractive summary → sentence-BERT embedding similarity score (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
C: Ensemble A+B with H174 dual filter (score≥0.18 + surprise≥0.02)
content.gate: OOS win-rate > 81.8% (H174 baseline) OR mean return > 6.89% (at n≥15 events)
content.cost_estimate: ~$0.04 per full backtest run (200 events); use Batch API for 50% discount (~$0.02). ~$0.0002/event standard pricing.
content.cost_note: GPT-4o-mini: $0.15/1M input, $0.60/1M output. ~700 tokens/call input, ~130 tokens output. Batch API recommended — no real-time requirement for backtests, eliminates rate-limit risk.
content.paper_note: Paper tests BART/FinBERT/LLaMA-3.2-3B on 10-Q MD&A (not 8-K, not GPT-4o-mini, not SBERT). H304 is a design extension, not a replication. Cite as: Hadlock et al. (2025), FinNLP @ EMNLP.
